However, human activities such as agriculture and forestry have drained roughly 15 percent of all peatland area since 1800, exposing the organic matter to oxygen and releasing significant amounts of carbon dioxide. While drainage suppresses microbial methane emissions, the net effect is a strong warming influence. According to a study published in *Nature* by MIT researchers and their collaborators, this historical and ongoing drainage accounts for about 2.7 percent of current human-caused global warming. The team combined worldwide drainage tracking data with new emission models to calculate these impacts. They warn that maintaining currently drained peatlands could almost double the cumulative warming caused by peatlands by 2100. Researchers emphasize that unlike deforestation where biomass emissions eventually stop, drained peatlands keep oxidizing and releasing carbon dioxide for centuries unless conservationists actively raise the water table back to its natural state.

item.title: Sakana AI Updates Marlin Agent with Twilight 2.0 and Midnight 2.0 Modes
item.description: According to Sakana AI: Background and Concept Launched in June, Sakana Marlin is designed as a strategic research agent that takes a research topic and autonomously handles everything from hypothesis generation to report writing. As user adoption grew, Sakana AI reports that users demanded higher standards for speed, depth, and breadth depending on their use cases. New Modes and Inference Scaling Building on the concept of inference-time scaling, Sakana AI introduces Twilight 2.0 and Midnight 2.0 alongside the existing Sunlight mode. The company states that Twilight 2.0 is built to quickly capture overall structures and broad overviews, while Midnight 2.0 focuses on deep exploration and rigorous verification, drawing on significantly more sources and generating longer reports. Redesigned Slide Output To help users grasp findings without reading full reports, Sakana AI has overhauled its PowerPoint export capability. A dedicated agent harness designs a coherent storyline, organizes quantitative data into charts, and formats the output into professional slide decks that follow corporate templates.

item.title: How to choose the next safe step in application modernization
item.description:
According to GitHub AI:
When modernizing old software, developers often face the dilemma of choosing a new framework without truly understanding the legacy system. Sam Quakenbush advocates collecting an evidence inventory first, which includes manifests, runtime pins, external contracts, and unverified assumptions. Instead of a full rewrite, he suggests a decision order ranging from keeping and upgrading to swapping, wrapping, or rewriting only when necessary.
To determine safety, teams can run a time-boxed feasibility check to either capture behavior before upgrading or build a modern slice first. Quakenbush applied this method across various public applications, from a small Node.js game to a large Java ERP system like ADempiere. Finally, these decision rules and safety levels can be encoded into a public agent skill for GitHub Copilot, helping structure modernization tasks while leaving final policy and approval to human system owners.

item.title: Schrödinger acquires Enpicom for 22 million euros to expand into biologics discovery
item.description:
Computational discovery biotech Schrödinger has finalized a deal to acquire Netherlands-based sequencing automation company Enpicom for 22 million euros, according to the companies. Schrödinger CEO Ramy Farid stated that the move allows the company to venture into biologics for the first time, having previously focused on small molecule drugs and advanced candidates currently in early-stage clinical trials.
Enpicom utilizes bioinformatics and artificial intelligence to speed up biologics discovery. Enpicom CEO Nicola Bonzanni noted that their software transforms weeks of complex sequence analysis into hours of decisive insights. The integration aims to combine Enpicom's software with Schrödinger's computational simulation platform to build an end-to-end infrastructure for future drug development modalities.

item.title: Cloudflare Introduces Search for Agents to Help AI Find Website Content Easily
item.description:
According to Cloudflare AI:
Cloudflare reports that setting up an AI search instance previously required manual configuration and complex integration work. According to Cloudflare, the new Search for Agents feature puts this entire setup behind a simple dashboard toggle, automatically crawling content and exposing standard APIs for AI agents.
Cloudflare explains that the system automatically advertises search endpoints within page metadata or Markdown headers. When an AI agent visits the site, it can immediately discover how and where to query information using natural language or keywords, receiving results directly in Markdown format rather than a pre-generated answer from another AI model.
Additionally, Cloudflare notes that the feature natively supports the new HTTP QUERY method (RFC 10008), allowing safe and idempotent requests with a request body. The service is available to all customers under standard AI Search pricing limits.

item.title: FDA issues noncompliance letters to 2 biotechs over lack of trial data reporting
item.description: According to Fierce Biotech, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued noncompliance letters to Duchesnay and Addex Pharma for failing to fulfill mandatory clinical trial reporting requirements. Background and Details Federal law requires that applicable clinical trial results be submitted to the ClinicalTrials.gov database, regardless of whether a study reached completion or was terminated early. The FDA began issuing such noncompliance notices in 2021 and has since sent a total of eleven letters to biopharmas, foundations, and investigators. In the latest batch sent in October, Duchesnay was cited for failing to report data regarding a phase 4 study targeting nausea and vomiting in pregnant teens, which was terminated in 2017 without a listed reason. Meanwhile, Addex Pharma received notices over a pair of Parkinson's disease trials, failing to submit results despite multiple emails exchanged with the agency since July 2025. Regulatory Implications Responsible parties are given 30 days after receiving a notice to take corrective action, failing which the FDA can pursue enforcement actions. The agency previously issued a similar letter to Mezzion Pharma in March 2025 concerning an un-reported pediatric heart surgery study, which was successfully resolved by January 2026 after the company addressed the outstanding issues.

item.title: Plant-based and cultivated meat patent filings decline amid industry pressures
item.description:
A new report from British IP firm Appleyard Lees reveals that priority patent filings for plant-based meat dropped from a revised 239 in 2023 to 187 in 2024, marking a nearly 22% decline and the third consecutive year of slowing activity. Similarly, cultivated meat patent applications fell by nearly 13% from 119 to 104, seeing declines for the second year running.
The data shows shifting geographic trends and corporate strategies. Europe saw a sharp drop in plant-based filings from 85 to 50, though it remains the most prolific region, while South Korea overtook the US in cultivated meat patent applications with 25 filings against the US's 20. Major consumer goods giants like Unilever and Nestlé scaled back their filing activities significantly, whereas companies like Cargill and dsm-firmenich bucked the trend.
Experts note that the downward trend reflects a more commercially focused phase. Rather than chasing pure scientific breakthroughs, remaining innovators are prioritizing lower-cost production, cell-culture methods, and improving taste, texture, and manufacturing efficiency to overcome ongoing commercialization hurdles.

item.title: UK Hospitals Cut Meal Emissions by 25% After Shift to Plant-Based Menus
item.description:
Medirest, the healthcare catering division of Compass Group, partnered with behavioural change organisation Greener by Default to test plant-rich menus across six British hospitals over a three-month period. Instead of imposing strict restrictions, the project applied behavioural science techniques by placing plant-based dishes at the top of menus and highlighting their flavors and origins rather than dietary labels.
According to the published results, the initiative led to an 8% shift from meat to plant-based meals, totaling 4,500 orders. This change reduced greenhouse gas emissions from main dishes by 22,000 kg of CO2e, marking a 25% reduction. Additionally, the trial recorded a 5% increase in overall meal uptake in staff and visitor restaurants, alongside a 39% rise in average fibre per meal and a 225% boost in legume intake. Medirest plans to use these insights to further develop its menus and expand recipe reformulation efforts.

item.title: LangChain introduces 'Agent Lake' to help developers improve AI agents at scale
item.description:
According to LangChain Blog:
As AI agents become more powerful and handle production workloads, manual debugging of agent traces no longer scales. According to Sam Crowder, LangChain is addressing this by converging its platform architecture toward an agent lake, mirroring how traditional data engineering uses data lakes.
The platform consists of two main pillars: a purpose-built database called SmithDB, which ingests billions of agent runs per month, and intelligent compute layers. SmithDB handles real-time trace data storage, while also capturing operational outcomes such as user feedback and merged pull requests to measure return on investment.
To process unstructured reasoning traces automatically, the intelligent compute layer provides automated tools like online evaluators, natural language AI Search, Insights for traffic analysis, LangSmith Engine for root cause diagnosis and automated pull requests, and SmithTune for fine-tuning custom models on top agent trajectories.

item.title: Anthropic allows users to install Claude-generated apps on Mac and Windows
item.description: How it Works According to Anthropic, the new "Install as app" feature allows users to take interactive artifacts created during a Claude chat and package them into dedicated desktop windows with their own icons. These installed apps can send notifications, integrate with system trays or menu bars, and automatically update whenever the original artifact is edited. Users can also share these apps with others via links, and the recipients can install them directly. Permissions and Security Apps operate under three permission levels, ranging from standard browser-like limits to full access where the app can run programs and modify files without prompting. Anthropic notes that it does not review these apps before installation, meaning full access should only be granted to trusted tools. Additionally, team and enterprise administrators can manage or restrict these permissions across their organizations.

item.title: Using AI to Write Obituaries Creates the Illusion of Meaning
item.description: The article discusses the increasing reliance on AI tools like Claude and ChatGPT to generate tributes, such as a recent political staffer's tribute to a music legend. The author argues that outsourcing tasks that require genuine human emotion strips away the flaws, personal memories, and true meaning of relationships. Even ChatGPT itself noted a distinction between using AI to express feelings versus manufacturing the appearance of them. The author concludes that if society starts outsourcing its most human experiences, it might be better to post nothing at all.

item.title: Behind the Nvidia case, a vast network diverting AI chips to China
item.description:
As Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang returned to lead the American chip giant, international financial media turned their attention to the methods enabling advanced processors to reach Chinese territory despite strict US export controls. These restrictions gained renewed urgency after Chinese startup DeepSeek unveiled a powerful AI system in January 2025, causing widespread concern in Washington.
When questioned in Taiwan in May 2025, Huang firmly denied any evidence of chip diversion. He pointed out that advanced AI systems are massive, weighing nearly two metric tons, making them impossible to slip into a pocket or backpack. Furthermore, Huang stated that tracking equipment is straightforward because companies and governments have a strong incentive to comply with orders and protect their supply chains if they want to keep buying from Nvidia in the future.

item.title: Yale expert says Nvidia is hurting U.S. industrial might
item.description:
In a recent interview, Yale business academic Jeffrey Sonnenfeld strongly criticized Nvidia’s board for caving to political pressure from the Trump administration and reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and board member. Sonnenfeld argued that the board showed extreme incompetence and cowardice by failing to use independent experts and reversing course after a brief investigation by the Wachtell law firm. He noted that unlike companies heavily dependent on government contracts, Nvidia relies very little on U.S. federal business, making the board's surrender indefensible.
Sonnenfeld also warned that Nvidia has become a detriment to U.S. industrial might, pointing to research showing that its most advanced chips have bypassed export controls and ended up in Chinese institutions and systems. Furthermore, he highlighted that the board's decisions and ongoing scandals are triggering massive legal fallout, including shareholder lawsuits, SEC probes, and antitrust investigations, which will likely cost the company and its directors dearly.

item.title: Xpeng boosts battery production as carmakers reduce reliance on CATL
item.description:
According to a local government social media post, Xpeng recently signed a 1.8 billion yuan (US$270 million) agreement with the Zhaoqing municipal government to build an integrated automotive project. This project includes new battery pack production lines with an annual capacity of 200,000 units, alongside new vehicle models and a global after-sales spare parts center.
Industry experts note that while in-house battery assembly offers limited direct cost savings, it helps automakers make cells more interchangeable and strengthens negotiating positions against dominant suppliers like CATL and BYD. Xpeng has already shifted most of its battery sourcing away from CATL in recent years, relying more on other suppliers, even as its net loss widened by 129 per cent year on year in the third quarter. Meanwhile, data from the China Automotive Battery Innovation Alliance shows CATL's market share in China's EV battery sector declined for six consecutive months, dropping to 40 per cent in October.

item.title: Anthropic Migrates Messages API from Python to Rust Using Autonomous Agents
item.description: According to Anthropic Research: Background and Challenge Anthropic built its Messages API in Python in 2023, but as API traffic grew significantly and safety classifiers, prompt tokenization, and multi-step streaming added overhead, Python became a performance bottleneck. While incremental rewrites only yielded minor gains, a full rewrite was traditionally considered too risky due to incomplete test suites and the difficulty of defining correctness for a live, changing system. Verification and Autonomous Agents To safely migrate the service without taking it offline, the team used the production system itself as an oracle. They set up a shadowing system that compared Python and Rust outputs on live traffic without reading private user data, utilizing checkpoints and fingerprints to isolate differences. Autonomous Claude agents operated within verification loops: a fast inner sandbox loop for iterative testing and a slower outer loop validating fixes against production traffic, while human engineers reviewed pull requests and guided policy. Results and Impact The migration reduced CPU usage per request by about 70% and cut the median time to first token by roughly 20%, all without freezing feature development or taking the service offline.

item.title: Germany Invests €35 Million to Build a 200-Qubit Silicon Quantum Computer
item.description: Project Background and Funding According to Forschungszentrum Jülich, the Jülich–Aachen spin-off ARQUE Systems has launched the Q-STAR.NRW initiative backed by a €35 million investment running through the end of 2029. The funding is provided 90% by German federal funds under the Coal Regions Investment Act and 10% by the State of North Rhine-Westphalia via Forschungszentrum Jülich. The resulting system will be deployed into the Jülich UNified Infrastructure for Quantum Computing at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre. Technology and Architecture Building on ARQUE Systems’ earlier five-qubit prototype, the new system encodes quantum information in the spins of individual electrons trapped in silicon and silicon-germanium structures. Instead of using traditional fixed couplings and dedicated control lines for every single qubit, the system utilizes a patented shuttling architecture that moves electrons to shared interaction zones. This design aims to significantly reduce wiring overhead and lay the groundwork for scaling beyond ten million qubits. Software and Applications In addition to hardware construction, the project partners will develop hybrid quantum-HPC software stacks and user support services to integrate the 200-qubit processor with classical supercomputers. This infrastructure will grant academic researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises access to test practical applications in materials science, chemistry, pharmaceuticals, and logistics.

item.title: MIT Energy Initiative reflects on 20 years of research and future challenges
item.description: According to MIT Climate: In a recent reflection on two decades of operations, MIT Energy Initiative Director William H. Green discussed the organization's evolution and impact since its founding in 2006. MITEI has brought nearly $1 billion in funding to MIT, fostering an active energy ecosystem that connects researchers with member companies to solve real-world problems. Green highlighted past successes, such as predicting electric vehicle market trends in a 2019 mobility study, and noted that MITEI-backed research has directly contributed to the creation of approximately 65 startup companies. Looking ahead, Green emphasized that the world faces major hurdles, including the need to decarbonize global systems responsible for three-quarters of greenhouse gas emissions while simultaneously meeting surging energy demands from artificial intelligence and expanding electrical access for populations worldwide.

item.title: Jensen Huang Tells Nvidia Staff Trump Didn't Get Him Rehired
item.description:
According to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and Marisa Kabas, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang addressed staff during his first all-hands meeting since returning to the company. Huang stated that claims of President Donald Trump playing a direct role in his reinstatement are completely untrue, insisting that politics did not influence the decision. He also dismissed the narrative that he returned because he felt above the law as a tech bro.
Huang apologized to staff for his actions, admitting he made terrible mistakes, was unfaithful to his wife, and hurt his family and employees. He noted that he is currently attending daily therapy and does not believe in succession planning. Meanwhile, Nvidia continues to face investigations regarding accounting practices and an internal probe into a reported Chinese spy plot, and Huang is set to testify before Congress on December 1st.

item.title: Arianespace Completes 10th Ariane 6 Flight and Plans Next Launch for December
item.description: Mission Details Arianespace successfully launched its Ariane 6 rocket from the Guiana Space Centre, deploying 36 Amazon Leo satellites into low Earth orbit at an altitude of approximately 460 kilometres. This flight marks the fourth mission for Amazon in 2026, bringing the total number of deployed satellites for their broadband constellation to 136. Technical Context and Schedule The launch follows the recent discovery and correction of an issue affecting one of the rocket's turbopumps. Although resolved for this flight, a further engine test is planned for early December to fully validate the fixes. The final Ariane 6 flight of 2026 is currently expected on 17 December, carrying a weather satellite for EUMETSAT.

item.title: Data Modeling Best Practices for an Agentic CDP, Part 1
item.description:
According to Databricks:
Databricks presents a comprehensive guide for data architects preparing data stacks for Agentic Customer Data Platforms (CDPs). Unlike traditional campaigns that target aggregated segments on a schedule, AI agents make real-time, individual-level decisions, requiring highly trustworthy and instantaneous data foundations. The Architecture The proposed flow utilizes a medallion architecture. Raw data lands in the bronze layer through connectors, followed by cleaning and normalization in the silver layer. Crucially, identity resolution runs immediately after the silver layer, combining deterministic rules and probabilistic matching to assign a persistent canonical ID. The gold layer then organizes this data into a core customer table, 1:1 attribute tables for model scores and consent, and 1:to-many behavior tables preserving event granularity. Practical Implementation Teams must flag each gold table as batch or event, utilizing streaming tables for real-time triggers like cart abandonment. By keeping the identity graph owned and auditable, brands ensure that agents make safe, compliant, and accurate customer decisions. Part two of the series will dive deeper into B2C and B2B dataset mapping and specific attribute use cases.

item.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
item.description: Looped Transformers increase expressivity by reusing shared layers across recurrent loops, but often suffer from efficiency bottlenecks. Lianghui Zhu et al. introduce the Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), featuring Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) which treats keys and values as memory for selective reuse. They propose variants including MoLT-R (retaining residual streams with cross-loop local KV) and MoLT-KV (restarting from embeddings and combining local KV with preceding-loop memory KV). To balance efficiency and prediction quality, they further develop U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals. In 400B-token pretraining experiments, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, yielding a 1.7x validation cross-entropy token efficiency gain at 700M. In a 100B-token continued pretraining run of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, the U-MoLT adaptation lowers cross-entropy across all 11 evaluated domains with 1.4x mean token efficiency. Code is publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: OS-Omni: Benchmarking Generalist Computer-Using Agents on Long-Horizon Workflows Across Platforms
item.description: The authors present OS-Omni, a live cross-platform benchmark and execution environment designed to evaluate computer-using agents on long-horizon workflows across Windows, Ubuntu, macOS, iOS, Android, and Web environments. Version 1 of the benchmark features 48 tasks per platform alongside 12 cross-platform workflows pairing desktops with Android phones, incorporating controlled service-backed applications with persistent state. Human baseline studies indicate that OS-Omni tasks require an average of 67.54 interaction steps, significantly longer than prior benchmarks such as OSWorld (15.0 steps). Experimental results on v1 show that the strongest evaluated agent, Claude Opus 5.5, achieves a 68.5% average success rate, trailing human performance by 8.8 points. Performance disparities vary considerably across platforms: while frontier models exceed human performance on Linux, they lag behind by more than 25 points on iOS and macOS, illustrating that current agents struggle with platform robustness, sustained state tracking, and durable final-state changes across heterogeneous operating systems.

item.title: Clearpath Introduces Husky A300 Mobile Robot Integrated with Fanuc Manipulator
item.description: According to Clearpath Robotics: System Overview and Integration Clearpath Robotics highlights a custom integration of the Husky A300, built as a flexible research and development platform. The system combines a mobile base with a robotic arm, end effector, wireless charging, and operator controls, offering a ready-to-use solution for autonomous systems. Key Components and Hardware The platform mounts a FANUC CRX-5iA collaborative robot arm featuring six axes of motion, a 5 kg payload, and a 994 mm reach. It uses a Robotiq adaptive gripper for handling objects of various shapes. Power is supplied by a 1 kW Wiferion wireless charging system that recharges the battery in two to three hours depending on the configuration. For control, a wired tablet with a magnetic mount provides operational access and an emergency stop interlock that halts both the base and the arm simultaneously.

item.title: Meta integrates Muse AI assistant directly into Instagram DMs
item.description: Meta announced on Tuesday that users can now chat with its Muse AI assistant directly within Instagram DM threads. This integration eliminates the need to toggle between Instagram and the standalone Muse app. According to Meta, users can share posts with Muse to ask questions about products or places, such as adding a coffee shop to a travel itinerary or finding shopping deals. Furthermore, users can now leverage Muse to organize their bookmarked posts and reels into custom folders known as Collections, or perform actions like turning recipe videos into grocery lists. Meta states that chat histories will sync as a side chat in the main Muse app. The feature starts rolling out on Tuesday for iOS and Android users in the U.S., Canada, Mexico, Japan, and Singapore, with the content organization feature specifically launching in the U.S. and Canada. Meta also emphasizes that users retain control, meaning nothing is shared or published without explicit approval, and users can request the AI to forget information at any time.

item.title: Mamdani questions AI economy as Jensen Huang returns to Nvidia
item.description:
According to Reuters and The Guardian, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani has weighed in on the corporate drama surrounding Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang. Mamdani stated that working Americans did not sign up to have their pensions tied to questions regarding Huang's marital fidelity.
Jensen Huang previously stepped down as CEO on November 12 following a reported extramarital relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, which triggered a dramatic drop in Nvidia's share price. Following subsequent pressure and political developments, Huang has now returned to the company, highlighting the fragile relationship between corporate tech leadership and national politics.

item.title: AMD Highlights Current Gaming Deals on CPUs, GPUs, and Systems
item.description: According to AMD Blogs: Deal Overview AMD reports a range of active gaming hardware discounts spanning CPUs, GPUs, laptops, desktops, and handheld devices. According to the company, these promotions feature strong value propositions anchored by popular Ryzen X3D processors starting at $379.99. Specific Offers and Conditions The hardware manufacturer points out that specific deals include products like the AMD Ryzen 7 9850X3D priced at $399.99 with an advertised $100 saving compared to standard pricing, though it is restricted to in-store pickup at select retailers like Micro Center. Additionally, the company notes that two distinct game bundles are available for customers making qualifying hardware purchases. Purchase Considerations While advertised savings are substantial across various configurations, consumers should note that actual availability varies by location. Certain offers may require specific promotional codes, backorders, or physical store visits to secure the discounted pricing.
